idea: Green hydrogen project economics modelling and research
buyer: Energy funds and developers assessing hydrogen projects
pain: Hydrogen project economics are widely misunderstood and mostly do not work
v1: A project economics model and honest assessment
verdict: Strong fit and honest positioning, but hydrogen enthusiasm and funding have cooled sharply.

why.demand: Inferred; hydrogen project activity has slowed and budgets with it.
why.fmf: Project economics modelling is squarely her skill; hydrogen technology specifics are not.
why.defensibility: Accumulated project comparisons help but specialist advisors compete.
why.leverage: Models and frameworks reuse across projects.
why.tailwind: Hydrogen has passed its hype peak and many projects are being cancelled.
why.ceiling: £16k x 12 projects = £192k, in a market where project count is falling.

ceiling_arithmetic: £16k x 12 projects = £192k. Hydrogen project volumes are contracting, so twelve engagements is unrealistic. Realistic: 3-4 = £48-64k.
carries: A genuine need for honest economics in a field full of optimistic assumptions.
kills: The market is shrinking. Being right about bad economics does not create a paying client base.
test: Ask three energy funds how many hydrogen projects they are still looking at.
